newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper squeeze to persist, prices seen firm.
newsitem.headline: LME copper squeeze to persist, prices seen firm.

text.p: Far East metal dealers said they expect the current squeeze on short positions in three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) to continue and push prices higher on the exchange later on Friday.
"Everybody's anticipating prices will be going higher. I believe the squeeze will continue," a Japanese dealer said.
Another trader said the contract's backwardation is likely to move in a range between US$170 and $220.
"It's going to be hard for the backwardation to come down. I think this will go on for another one or two weeks," he said.

"The scramble to cover short positions continued as concern grew that the technical tightness would intensify and could approach levels last seen in January of over $300 backwardation ahead of the tight dates still to come in late April/early May," LME brokers Brandeis said in its daily review.

But another European dealer said he felt the recent rise in copper was overdone. "I'm going to stick my neck out and say you'll find a lot of profit-taking today. Copper is going to come down a bit," the trader said.
Three month copper was seen by the trade at 0230 GMT at around $2,365/70 a tonne, little changed from the late London indication on Thursday of $2,366/70.
Traders said they have discounted reports quoting the union leader of 358 striking workers at the Escondida mine in northern Chile saying that it is running short of copper concentrates.
"We'd like to see more solid information first," one said.
The mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ-CRA.
But the trade is monitoring possible stoppages at other mines, maintenance work at Kennecott Corp's smelter in Utah, and a reduction in the April output of Zambia's state-owned ZCCM.
"Low global stocks, tight physical markets and supply-side concerns are exacerbating the situation, providing a short term boost to prices," Brandeis said.
LME copper inventories are seen dipping by another 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes when the stocks report is issued at 0800 GMT.

Dealers here are monitoring stocks in the LME's Singapore warehouse to see if these will fall anew. The volume of copper in the city-state reached 23,875 tonnes yesterday, down 1,375 tonnes from Wednesday's report.
